\section{Introduction}
When two finite bodies exchange heat, energy conservation fixes the temperature they can ultimately share, while the contact law determines how quickly they approach it. Both bodies change temperature, so neither can generally be treated as an unchanged thermal bath. An elementary two-reservoir calculation makes these distinct roles explicit.

We consider an isolated pair with constant heat capacities and a linear thermal contact. The temperature difference decays exponentially, and the conserved energy determines a common final temperature. The same trajectory keeps both temperatures positive and produces a nonnegative total entropy change without requiring a small initial temperature difference. These conclusions concern the stipulated equations; their exact solution does not establish their accuracy for a particular physical apparatus.
